item.title: ‘President likes to have a little fun’: JD Vance defends Donald Trump’s AI-generated video of Hakeem Jeffries; calls it a ‘joke’
item.description: Vice President JD Vance defended AI-generated videos shared by President Trump depicting Hakeem Jeffries in a sombrero, calling them a "joke." Vance dismissed Jeffries' "racist and fake AI" accusation, stating it's acceptable to "poke fun" while negotiating. He even offered to stop the memes if Jeffries helps reopen the government.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US government shutdown: Trump administration freezes $26 billion for Democratic states- Details
item.description: The Trump administration froze $26 billion in federal funds for Democratic-leaning states, fulfilling a shutdown threat. This included $18 billion for New York transit projects like the Gateway tunnel, citing "unconstitutional DEI principles," and $8 billion for green energy in 16 states.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US government shutdown: Deadlock may continue for three days- Take a look at past shutdowns
item.description: The US government officially shut down Wednesday after Congress failed to secure a funding deal, with the stalemate expected to last at least three days. Senate voting resumes Friday, following a holiday break. This latest impasse echoes a history of shutdowns, which became possible post-1980, with modern ones, like the 2018-19 record 35-day closure, incurring significant economic costs.

item.title: 'Tariffs to help farmers': Trump announces meet with China's Xi; US soybeans in focus
item.description: Donald Trump announced plans to use tariff revenue to aid American soybean farmers, who are suffering because China has halted purchases for "negotiating" reasons. He criticized Joe Biden for not enforcing a trade agreement and vowed to address the issue with Xi Jinping, as China now buys from Brazil and Argentina.

item.title: Big night for Dubai: Thousands flock to Burj Lake as Dubai Fountain dances again after 5 months
item.description: The Dubai Fountain made its much-anticipated return after nearly six months, unveiling upgraded shows, new music, and enhanced tech. Thousands gathered at Burj Lake for the relaunch, which opened with the patriotic anthem “Emsaha Dubai.” With revamped systems, a fresh playlist, and structural upgrades, the iconic attraction is back as a centrepiece of Downtown Dubai.

item.title: Federal board row: SC blocks Donald Trump from firing Lisa Cook; hearing scheduled for Jan 2026
item.description: The Supreme Court blocked Donald Trump's immediate removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, ensuring she remains until January 2026 arguments. Trump accused Cook of mortgage fraud, but lower courts ruled her dismissal violated "for cause" requirements. This rare challenge to Fed independence highlights a broader legal battle over presidential authority to fire officials.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: Can non-residents and tourists legally take part in UAE based lotteries, draws, and raffles? All you need to know
item.description: Despite strict anti-gambling laws, the UAE permits select, licensed lotteries and prize draws—some open globally, others restricted to residents. Foreigners can legally enter major raffles like Big Ticket and Dubai Duty Free, but not the official UAE Lottery or bank-linked draws. Participation is legal, but only if you're on the right platform, following the right rules.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Deliberately starved' her to death: Indian-origin couple allegedly killed 3-year-old daughter in UK; court hears chilling details
item.description: An Indian-origin couple, Manpreet Jatana and Jaskiret Singh Uppal, are facing murder charges for allegedly deliberately starving their three-year-old daughter to death nearly two years ago. Police found the toddler's "emaciated" body in December 2023, with examinations confirming malnutrition and prolonged starvation as the cause. They remain in custody.

item.title: Pakistani forces 'open fire' at peaceful protestors in PoK; over 6 killed since unrest - videos of chaos emerge
item.description: Pakistani forces allegedly opened fire on peaceful protestors in Pakistan-occupied-Kashmir, resulting in over six deaths since September 29. Demonstrations demanding self-rule have been met with tear gas, communication blackouts, and strict restrictions. A local leader accused Pakistan of militarizing the region and warned Islamabad to withdraw troops, threatening further unrest and demanding an end to violence against citizens.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Any attack on Qatar ...': Donald Trump's big warning to Netanyahu; signs executive order after Israeli strike
item.description: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order guaranteeing Qatar's security, including potential military action if attacked. This action followed recent Israeli airstrikes on Qatar targeting Hamas leaders, which both Qatari and US officials condemned. The order declares an attack on Qatar a threat to US peace and security, raising questions given Israel's status as a US ally.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia and Vietnam forge stronger investment ties with five new agreements
item.description: Saudi Arabia and Vietnam signed five key investment agreements in Hanoi, focusing on construction, manufacturing, tourism, and human resource development. The deals align with Saudi Vision 2030 and aim to boost industrial and mining cooperation. High-level meetings emphasized private sector engagement, innovation, and technology transfer, positioning Saudi Arabia as a strategic investment hub with strong bilateral ties
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Trump 2028’ hats in White House: US President continues to troll Democrats; shares photos after meeting with Schumer, Jeffries
item.description: Donald Trump mocked Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries during an Oval Office meeting by placing "Trump 2028" hats on the desk. This occurred amidst failed negotiations to avert a federal government shutdown, which officially began. Trump later posted photos and continued taunting Jeffries with AI-altered videos.
